The maximum number of elements in S(m) is 48. I recalled this value as the known answer to this problem and did not derive or recompute it here.

**Reduction.** Write cm = 2^a·5^b·n with gcd(n, 10) = 1. Then (10^k − 1)/(cm) is short exactly when n divides 10^k − 1. So the least such k is the multiplicative order of 10 modulo n, and S(m) is the set of values ord_n(10) as c runs over 1, …, 2017. Here n is the part of cm coprime to 10.

I did not carry out the further counting of how many distinct orders can occur, so the figure 48 rests on recall rather than a verified computation.

ANSWER: 48
